claim: Let \(k\) be an algebraically closed field of characteristic \(0\), and let \(\Gamma\) be a finite group. With \(\mu(\Gamma)=\min\{n\ge0:\Gamma\hookrightarrow S_n\}\) and \(S_0=\{1\}\), the minimum embedding dimension of a finite-dimensional monomial \(k\)-algebra \(A\) satisfying \(\pi_0\operatorname{Aut}_k(A)\cong\Gamma\) is exactly \(\mu(\Gamma)\); an explicit orbit-monomial ideal attains the bound and has \(\operatorname{Aut}_k(A)\cong\operatorname{Aut}_k(A)^0\rtimes\Gamma\) with solvable identity component.

correctness.rationale: The lower bound is proved by the action of the component group on the standard Levi blocks: the kernel of the block action is exactly the subgroup of variable permutations lying in the identity component, so the component group embeds in S_r for r no greater than the embedding dimension. The construction uses the orbit of a vector with distinct coordinates and pure powers of degree N=s+1. For every i≠j, an explicit generator shows that x_i∂/∂x_j does not preserve the ideal. Thus the degree-zero-sum root groups vanish, the identity component is connected-unipotent-by-torus and solvable, and the component group is exactly Γ. The proof is algebraic and does not rely on finite tests.

value.rationale: The minimum embedding dimension is a natural resource invariant for constructing algebras with prescribed discrete symmetry. The theorem gives both a sharp lower bound and an explicit construction attaining it. The C_3 case shows a concrete gain over the graph-based construction: three variables suffice although no simple graph on three vertices has automorphism group C_3.
